root_idea.summary: The attested semantic center is the cessation of flame, heat, or fire, or the causing of these to cease.
root_idea.development: The lexical record shows an intransitive fire becoming extinguished alongside the causative act of extinguishing it, with figurative and specialized extensions built on the same extinction imagery.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form IV perfect citation form أَطْفَأَ.

senses.definition: To extinguish or quench a fire; figuratively, to suppress an active conflict or similar force.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive Form IV. The Quran applies the verb to putting out a fire kindled for war and figuratively to attempting to extinguish the light of God; these are applications of the same extinguishing construction, not separate light-specific senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a fire: to become extinguished or quenched, ceasing to flame; in the stricter description, its live coals have also cooled.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The lexical distinction recorded here separates a fire whose flame has merely died down while its coals still burn from one whose flame and coals are fully extinct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A traditional name for one of the seven days called أَيَّامُ العَجُوز, associated with extinguishing the last live coal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The day is variously reported as the fourth or the fifth of the series.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of fat that melts on heated stones and quenches them; also, in an associated expression, a sheep or goat slaughtered in a way described as quenching those stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cited lexical accounts variously describe the animal as lean or fat.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A serpent whose poison is said to extinguish a fire as it passes over heated stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a specialized Classical usage connected with the serpent’s effect on heated stones.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A calamity or misfortune, figuratively conceived as something that makes what came before forgotten and extinguishes its heat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage based on the extinction of heat and the displacement of what preceded it.
